title: Request to General Assembly (re: Teaching Elder from Western Carolina Presbytery)
disposition_detail: The SJC held the three presbyteries’ BCO 34-1 requests administratively out of order and not properly before the General Assembly. Original jurisdiction was not assumed, and no further proceedings were ordered.
first_summary: Three presbyteries asked the General Assembly to assume original jurisdiction over a minister allegedly responsible for women preaching from a church pulpit. The SJC dismissed the matter because worship fell under the Session’s jurisdiction and Tennessee Valley Presbytery had not refused to act: it had adopted resolutions addressing the controversy. The SJC therefore did not reach the merits of the allegations under BCO 34-1.
summary: Three presbyteries asked the General Assembly under BCO 34-1 to assume original jurisdiction over a minister alleged to have allowed women to preach from a church pulpit. The SJC held the requests administratively out of order and did not reach the allegation’s merits. Worship was the Session’s responsibility, so the minister could not be held liable for actions assigned to it; moreover, Tennessee Valley Presbytery had acted on the allegations, defeating BCO 34-1’s refusal-to-act prerequisite. No further proceedings were ordered.
